title: The missing herd
lines: The herd has not returned, and a convincing story will not feed the camp.
Beyond the Last Stone begins with a prehistoric community facing hunger and an uncertain route forward.

emotionalPlan.purpose: Open on the camp and absent herd signs, keeping hunger concrete without sensational distress.
voiceDirections: Speak with restrained urgency; give gentle emphasis to will not feed the camp. Keep a natural conversational voice, let the listener picture this specific situation, and leave a real pause at the end.

title: Which signs can guide us?
lines: Ar, a young hunter, asks what people have actually seen; others remember what stories can carry.
They must decide together before anyone can be sure which signs to trust.

emotionalPlan.purpose: Retain tracks and attentive human gestures; do not resolve which route is right.

title: Thought beside the fire
lines: Through tracks, counting stones, and fireside arguments, the novel makes early ideas about knowledge feel immediate.
Its people need knowledge, but they also need courage, shared memory, and one another.

emotionalPlan.purpose: Use one counting-stone movement beside the fire instead of teaching the later conceptual discovery.
voiceDirections: Speak with lively warmth; give gentle emphasis to fireside arguments. Keep a natural conversational voice, let the listener picture this specific situation, and leave a real pause at the end.
Speak with human warmth; give gentle emphasis to one another. Keep a natural conversational voice, let the listener picture this specific situation, and leave a real pause at the end.

title: Join the River People
lines: The adventure is discovering how an idea can guide a life without becoming a certainty.
Join the River People at the first hungry camp, where every claim has somewhere to lead.
